title: Have We Reached "Peak Marketplace" in Southeast Asia Ecommerce?
summary: Marketplaces drive 70% of Southeast Asia ecommerce, but take rates have tripled and AI is moving the first click. Which channel posture will you take?
body_markdown:
*Southeast Asia is one of the most marketplace-concentrated ecommerce markets in the world: About 70% of online sales take place on marketplaces, up from around 40% a decade ago, and brands have done well out of it. But the cost of being there has risen sharply, and the way shoppers begin their journey is starting to change. We do not think the peak is here yet, but it is closer than ever, and that forces a decision on every merchant in the region: Which channel posture do you want to be in when it arrives?*


For ten years, people in Southeast Asian ecommerce have asked the same question: When does the straw break the camel's back? Every year the marketplaces take a bigger share of sales and a bigger cut of each sale, and every year industry participants, including us, predict that sellers will eventually walk. So far, we have been wrong. This year, two things look different.


## **Southeast Asia ecommerce is built on marketplaces**


Today, about 70% of Southeast Asia's ecommerce sales take place on marketplaces, according to the[Xendit Ecommerce Payments](https://www.xendit.co/en/ecomms-momentum-report/?utm_source=mag-event&utm_medium=booth&utm_campaign=ecomms-momentum-repo)[Momentum Report 2026](https://www.xendit.co/en/ecomms-momentum-report/?utm_source=mag-event&utm_medium=booth&utm_campaign=ecomms-momentum-repo) . That is level with South Korea, above India at around 65% and far above Latin America at around 40%. Only China, at around 85%, is higher.


The marketplaces earned that position. They solved, in one place, the things a brand would otherwise have to solve alone:


- Assortment and traffic: Shoppers go to the marketplace first, so that is where the demand is


- Prices and promotions, much of it subsidized by the platforms themselves


- Logistics, payments and fraud handling, which in the early years were hard for a brand to arrange on its own


But the deal has always been the same. You do not own your home. You rent, and the landlord keeps the customer data, sets the rules of the shop and decides how much to reinvest.


## **What has changed: The rent and the first click**


### **1. The rent has tripled**


Take Shopee, the region's largest marketplace, as the example. Its take rate, meaning the commission, advertising and service fees it collects on each sale, went from around 4% in 2019 to nearly 13% in 2026. The other platforms have moved in the same direction. And that is just the baseline fees:


- Shopee's commission alone went from 2.2% to 8.3% of sales


- The nominally optional costs, free shipping programs, marketing contributions and logistics contributions, have risen too, and in most categories you effectively cannot sell without them


- All in, our client work suggests the cost of trading on a marketplace now often lands at 20 to 30% of sales


In retrospect, the rent was too low. Southeast Asia has been a cheaper place to sell through a marketplace than almost any mature market, and it will probably stay below the United States. The problem is less the level than the experience: Merchants saw little additional value for the extra money, and there was nowhere else to sell, or at least nowhere to hedge their reliance on the platforms.


### **2. The first click is moving**


The marketplaces' real advantage was never the fees they charge. It was that so many shopping journeys started in their app. That grip is loosening:


- Southeast Asian consumers are among the most social in the world, and many journeys already begin on Instagram, YouTube or TikTok rather than in a marketplace search bar


- Generative AI is quickly moving to the front of the journey. In our survey of 6,000 shoppers, 78% use generative AI during product research, ahead of search engines at 74%, and 53% already use it during discovery


- When an assistant answers "which one should I buy, and where", the shopper stops caring whether the answer is Shopee or the brand's own site


- The platforms can see it coming. In September, for example, Amazon blocked Meta's Muse shopping agent from its store. Shopify, which powers brand sites, welcomed it


## **What the platforms still have going for them**


The platforms are not standing still. Shopee, Lazada and TikTok Shop together grew 33% year on year in the first quarter of 2026, faster than the rest of the market. Part of that is TikTok Shop, a different kind of commerce, social and live, and less exposed to the forces above. Part of it is logistics: Nobody outside Shopee's SPX network offers the same same-day coverage. And off-platform traffic at scale is still unproven.


Payments are a good example of the convenience the platforms offer, and of what a merchant gives up for it. Inside a marketplace, the platform decides the checkout, which payment methods are on offer, how cash on delivery and refunds work and how fraud is screened. The merchant gets little say and little visibility, with the cost built into the take rate.


Outside, those decisions become the merchant's own, and they matter: In our shopper survey, a preferred payment method not being available is the top reason for abandoning a purchase in Indonesia (51%), the Philippines (41%) and Malaysia (31%). And there is no single regional payment mix to build for. E-wallets lead in Indonesia, cards in Singapore, bank transfers in Thailand, and cash on delivery still accounts for close to a quarter of ecommerce value in the Philippines.


So what would the tipping point look like? Not exactly platforms shrinking, but rather platforms growing slower than the rest of ecommerce for the first time. That is the number to watch.


## **The decision: Which posture will you take?**


For ecommerce leaders at brands and retailers, the question is not whether the peak lands in 2027 or 2029. It is which of three postures to be in when it does, because each has consequences and each takes time to build.


- **Marketplace-only.** Lowest effort and highest reach, with the platforms carrying logistics, payments and fraud. The trade-off: Margins that move with the platform's fee schedule, no customer data, and when an AI agent decides where to buy, only one place for it to go. Fits low price points, impulse categories and brands without strong pull of their own.


- **Hybrid.** Marketplaces for reach and acquisition; an owned channel, brand.com or e-retail, for repeat purchase, bundles, exclusives, data and margin. The trade-off: Two P&Ls to run, a traffic engine to build and a checkout that has to match local payment habits in every market. The reward is leverage: A seller with somewhere else to go negotiates differently, and gives AI agents a second door. This is where we expect most large merchants to land.


- **Full direct-to-consumer.** Full control and full margin, with traffic, logistics, payments and fraud carried alone. In Southeast Asia today this works for a short list: Retailers, high price points, brands people search for by name, and products where the purchase journey is only about buying that product.


Whichever posture a brand chooses, the numbers behind it have moved. Commerce platforms, payment providers and logistics networks outside the marketplaces have matured considerably in the last few years, so a business case that did not work in 2022 may well work now. It is worth revisiting.


*Simon Torring, Co-Founder of Cube Asia, at a media roundtable in Jakarta presenting the report findings.*


The findings in this article come from the[Xendit Ecommerce Payments](https://www.xendit.co/en/ecomms-momentum-report/?utm_source=mag-event&utm_medium=booth&utm_campaign=ecomms-momentum-repo)[Momentum Report 2026](https://www.xendit.co/en/ecomms-momentum-report/?utm_source=mag-event&utm_medium=booth&utm_campaign=ecomms-momentum-repo)


, published by Cube Asia and Xendit and launched on October 15, 2026, at The Langham, Jakarta, and Shangri-La The Fort, Manila.


The full report covers market growth, marketplace economics, how shoppers pay across six Southeast Asian markets, the arrival of agentic commerce and five predictions for 2027.
